ACTION: ADD 1
TITLE: Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: We propose fine-tuning a pre-trained VFM by generating adversarial perturbations to the input images, while matching the output distributions of the model. Specifically, we will employ the adaptive adversary (ADA) to generate the perturbations, and Vanilla Jayaraman Neville (VJN) minimax loss function to maintain the output consistency under perturbations.
CONTROLS: Supervised fine-tuning, SimCLR (SimClr).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method can provide a robust adaptation without the need for any labeled data. However, its effectiveness might be limited when the pre-trained model has weak representations, and may not generalize well to significantly different domains.

ACTION: ADD 2
TITLE: Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We explore incorporating both spatial and temporal context of unlabeled multi-view videos to adapt a pre-trained VFM. We utilize a cross-modal contrastive learning framework where we learn to distinguish the video representations from different views, while encouraging the model to focus on common features across views.
CONTROLS: Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning (Proposal 1), Supervised fine-tuning.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This approach may improve upon Proposal 1 by leveraging more context information from videos, and its robustness can lead to stable learning even in poorly initialized networks. Nevertheless, comparing how these methods scale to different domain similarity remains an open question.

ACTION: ADD 3
TITLE: Unsupervised Visual Attribute Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: We propose to fine-tune a pre-trained VFM by learning to predict visual attributes from unlabeled data that are heavily correlated with the task-specific attributes of interest. This allows us to tap into the pre-trained model's knowledge without needing any labeled data for the target task.
CONTROLS: Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Supervised fine-tuning.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method may struggle to capture nuanced task-specific attributes and can be sensitive to the quality of the attributes used. However, it can potentially recover the pre-trained representations if the attributes are well-aligned with the task requirements.

ACTION: REVISE 2
TITLE: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning
PROPOSAL: We modify the video-based framework to better capture the object-centric information in multi-view videos by incorporating an object masking module that suppresses irrelevant background pixels and enhances the spatial consistency of the features. This enables more targeted and effective learning from the video data.
CONTROLS: Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning (Proposal 1), Supervised fine-tuning, Unsupervised Visual Attribute Transfer Learning (Proposal 3).
COST: Revised: 150 GPU-hours (for mask fine-tuning)
PREDICTION: This revised method should be more effective at capturing relevant object-centric features, but its enhanced complexity may make it more susceptible to overfitting in low-data regimes.

ACTION: ADD 4
TITLE: Uncertainty-guided Dynamic Weight Averaging for Unsupervised Fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: We adapt a recently proposed technique, dynamic weight averaging (DWA), for unsupervised fine-tuning to adjust the weights of the pre-trained model based on confidence scores of the predictions. Specifically, we use an uncertainty estimate (e.g., Monte Carlo dropout) to compute the confidence scores and dynamically weigh the model weights between the pre-trained and fine-tuned representations.
CONTROLS: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Supervised fine-tuning, Unsupervised Visual Attribute Transfer Learning (Proposal 3).
COST: 110 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method may provide a robust way to adapt to uncertain data and can help the model adapt more gradually, but its dependence on estimating uncertainty might be challenging in cases where data quality is poor.

ACTION: ADD 5
TITLE: Per-Pixel randomized Decoherence Dataset Augmentation (P2R-DDA)
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel dataset augmentation method that combines random pixel-wise transformations with decoherence techniques from quantum computing. By reorganizing the pixel structure of images, this approach can effectively decorrelate features and improve the representational capacity of the pre-trained model, enabling more robust fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Supervised fine-tuning, Unsupervised Visual Attribute Transfer Learning (Proposal 3).
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This novel approach may effectively enhance the pre-trained representations by increasing the variability of the data, but its effectiveness might be diminished in cases where the number of training images is limited due to excessive overfitting.

ACTION: REVISE 1
TITLE: REVISED Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning
PROPOSAL: We enhance the Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning (APO) method by incorporating an adaptive temperature schedule and a corrected loss function that better balances exploration and exploitation during the fine-tuning process. This modification is aimed at stabilizing the convergence of the model and preventing it from prematurely converging to an inadequate solution.
CONTROLS: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Uncertainty-guided Dynamic Weight Averaging for Unsupervised Fine-tuning (Proposal 4), Supervised fine-tuning.
COST: Revised: 130 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised approach may improve the effectiveness and robustness of the APO method by adapting the exploration-exploitation trade-off during fine-tuning, but its performance might still suffer if the pre-trained model lacks strong initial representations.

ACTION: ADD 6
TITLE: Contrastive Decorrelation of Early Representations
PROPOSAL: We propose a novel technique to contrastively decorrelate the early representations of the pre-trained model by encouraging the activation values of early layers to be decorrelated from the labels, which helps to relax the dependency on the specific learning objectives.
CONTROLS: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Supervised fine-tuning, REVISED Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning (Proposal 1).
COST: 90 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This method may help to detoxify the early representations by making them less sensitive to the loss functions designed for specific tasks, potentially leading to more transferable and robust features that are better suited for adaptation. However, its effect on pre-trained weights will depend on the specific initial conditions of the model.

ACTION: ADD 7
TITLE: Episodic Training for Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Experience Replay
PROPOSAL: We propose to incorporate an episodic training framework with experience replay into the pre-training task, utilizing the unlabeled target domain data to select episodes of relevant instances and adaptively modify the pre-trained model through self-supervised learning, which can help in efficient fine-tuning of the pre-trained model to specific tasks.
CONTROLS: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Supervised fine-tuning, REVISED Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning (Proposal 1).
COST: 180 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This episodic training approach with experience replay may enable faster learning and more adaptive fine-tuning of the pre-trained model by incorporating memory-based decisions that are adaptive to the target domain, which can lead to better generalization but may struggle with catastrophic forgetting.

ACTION: REVISE 3
TITLE: REVISED Unsupervised Visual Attribute Transfer Learning
PROPOSAL: We modify the Unsupervised Visual Attribute Transfer Learning (UVATL) approach by incorporating a hybrid label-attribute learning module that enhances the representation learning from visual attributes, which facilitates more effective adaptation of pre-trained representations to the target domain.
CONTROLS: REVISED Video-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Cross-modal Contrastive Learning (Proposal 2), Supervised fine-tuning, REVISED Adversarial Perturbation-based Unsupervised Fine-tuning (Proposal 1), Episodic Training for Unsupervised Fine-tuning with Experience Replay (Proposal 7).
COST: Revised: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: This revised UVATL approach may strike a balance between guidance from pre-trained attributes and adaptability to new data distributions, but its success will depend on the quality of the attribute features and the representational capacity of the pre-trained model.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating Supervision Sensitivity in Unsupervised Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Compare the performance of unsupervised fine-tuning of a pre-trained visual foundation model (e.g., DINO) on unlabeled real-world object-centric video data versus additional fine-tuning with noisy labels, weak labels, or semi-supervised learning objectives.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - no added fine-tuning; ablation 2 - additional fine-tuning with only noise labels.
COST: 50 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect unsupervised fine-tuning to perform competitively with weak labels, but both methods to struggle with noisy labels that are consistently misaligned with the true labels. Lessons from this study can inform the choice of added supervision for unsupervised fine-tuning, reducing the reliance on expensive or impractical labeled data.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Investigation of Input Space Smoothing to Mitigate Distribution Shifts During Unsupervised Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Evaluate the performance of unsupervised fine-tuning for vision foundation models with input space smoothing (ISS) -- a technique that involves data augmentation and feature selection to reduce the effective dimensionality of input space, potentially mitigating distribution shifts.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - ISS disabled; ablation 2 - ISS with random feature removal; ablation 3 - ISS with spatial smoothing (e.g., Gaussian blur).
COST: 30 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We hypothesize that ISS will help stabilize the training process and maintain the pretrained knowledge during unsupervised fine-tuning, potentially improving performance in the target domain. However, the efficacy of ISS may depend on the specific domain and distribution shifts involved.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Video-based Temporal Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Introduce temporal contrastive learning as a new self-supervised objective for unsupervised fine-tuning of vision foundation models on videos. This involves extracting temporal features from videos using 3D convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and then learning to distinguish between different temporal contexts using a contrastive loss.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - no temporal contrastive learning; ablation 2 - temporal contrastive learning with a fixed temporal context window.
COST: 70 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect temporal contrastive learning to provide a robust and domain-invariant signal that can help the model adapt to the target domain without explicit supervision, especially for vision-centric encoder models. However, the choice of temporal context window and the trade-off between self-supervision and fine-tuning may require further exploration.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Evaluating Supervision Sensitivity in Unsupervised Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models
REVISED PROPOSAL: Instead of using noise labels or weak labels, modify the study to evaluate the use of pseudo-labels generated by a separate, simpler model (e.g., a lightweight CNN) trained on a subset of the target domain data. Compare the performance of unsupervised fine-tuning with these pseudo-labels to the baseline pre-trained VFM.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - no added fine-tuning; ablation 2 - fine-tuning with pseudo-labels from a lightweight CNN.
COST: 40 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect pseudo-labels to provide a useful signal for unsupervised fine-tuning, although the performance may depend on the quality of the lightweight model and the amount of data used for pseudo-label generation. Lessons from this study can inform the choice of pseudo-label generation strategies and the trade-off between pseudo-label quality and fine-tuning performance.

ACTION: REVISE
TITLE: Video-based Temporal Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Fine-Tuning
REVISED PROPOSAL: Modify the temporal contrastive learning objective to incorporate visual transformer layers to better model the complex spatial-temporal relationships in the videos. Additionally, experiment with different loss functions (e.g., InfoNCE, Triplet) and temperature scaling to adapt the contrastive learning to the specific domain.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - visual transformer layer disabled; ablation 2 - different loss functions.
COST: 80 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the visual transformer modification to improve the model's ability to learn domain-invariant representations, and that the choice of loss function and temperature scaling will play a crucial role in adapting the model to the target domain.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Transfer Learning with Video-Augmented Pseudotargets for Unsupervised Fine-Tuning
PROPOSAL: Provide additional supervision to the unsupervised fine-tuning process by using video-augmented pseudotargets -- synthesized images that mimic the visual structure and motion of real-world videos. Evaluate the performance of fine-tuning on these pseudotargets versus other forms of unsupervised fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - pseudotargets disabled; ablation 2 - pseudotargets generated using a different method (e.g., adversarial model, 3D generative model).
COST: 100 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect video-augmented pseudotargets to provide a useful signal for unsupervised fine-tuning, especially for models that struggle to adapt to the target domain. However, the quality of the pseudotargets and the trade-off between added supervision and fine-tuning performance may require further exploration.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Multi-modal Self-Supervision for Unsupervised Fine-Tuning of Vision Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Explore the use of multi-modal self-supervision -- combining multiple self-supervision tasks (e.g., temporal contrastive learning, visual transformer self-supervision, input space smoothing) to learn more robust and domain-invariant representations.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - single self-supervision task; ablation 2 - different combinations of self-supervision tasks.
COST: 120 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect multi-modal self-supervision to improve the model's ability to learn domain-invariant representations, especially when combining tasks that are complementary in their strengths. However, careful selection and weighting of the self-supervision tasks will be crucial to avoid overwhelming the model with conflicting signals.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Robustness Analysis of Unsupervised Fine-Tuning for Vision Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Investigate the robustness of unsupervised fine-tuning to variations in hyperparameters, model architectures, and data quality -- factors that are known to affect supervised fine-tuning performance. Analyze the sensitivity of the model to these variations and identify key factors that impact performance.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; hyperparameter sweep (e.g., learning rate, batch size, number of epochs); model architecture modifications (e.g., changing the number of layers or filters); data quality variations (e.g., changing the amount of data or corruption levels).
COST: 200 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the model to be relatively robust to variations in hyperparameters and model architectures, but sensitive to data quality variations. Understanding the model's robustness will inform the design of more reliable unsupervised fine-tuning protocols.

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Evaluating the Generalizability of Unsupervised Fine-Tuning Across Domains
PROPOSAL: Investigate the transferability of unsupervised fine-tuning to novel object recognition tasks in multi-view object-centric videos across different domains (e.g., cars, animals, household objects) and camera views. Evaluate the model's ability to generalize across domains without explicit fine-tuning.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - no fine-tuning; ablation 2 - fine-tuning on a different domain (e.g., fine-tuning on animals after pre-training on cars).
COST: 300 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the model to exhibit good transferability across domains, especially when the domains share similar visual properties (e.g., objects with similar shapes and textures), but may struggle with domains that are significantly different (e.g., fine-tuning on images of animals after pre-training on images of cars).

ACTION: ADD
TITLE: Unsupervised Fine-Tuning with Label-Hallucination for Vision Foundation Models
PROPOSAL: Introduce a new approach to unsupervised fine-tuning that incorporates a label-hallucination mechanism -- a model that hallucinates labels for the target domain based on its self-supervised knowledge. Evaluate the performance of this approach versus other unsupervised fine-tuning methods.
CONTROLS: Baseline - pre-trained VFM; ablation 1 - no label-hallucination; ablation 2 - different variants of label-hallucination (e.g., multi-modal hallucination, attention-based hallucination).
COST: 350 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect label-hallucination to provide a strong signal for unsupervised fine-tuning, especially when combined with other self-supervision methods, but the hallucination mechanism may introduce errors or biases that need to be addressed.

ACTION: REVISE 1
title: exploring image-wise contrastive learning for unsupervised fine-tuning of vfms
PROPOSAL: Investigate the effect of incorporating spatial and temporal augmentations into the image-wise contrastive learning of proposal 1. This can be done by manipulating the input video frames to introduce temporal shifts, and applying random crops or flips to the individual frames. Evaluate how the different augmentations influence the model's performance on object recognition tasks.
CONTROLS: Baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning without augmentations)
COST: estimated additional 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: Incorporating temporal augmentations improves performance on object recognition tasks, mainly due to increased robustness against temporal variations in the videos; however, spatial augmentations may have a diminishing effect on performance due to the redundancy of visual information across frames.

action: add
title: video discriminator for self-supervised pretraining
proposal: Explore the use of video discriminators as a component of self-supervised pretraining for visual foundation models. Implement a discriminator that takes videos as input and outputs a confidence score for each frame being part of a coherent sequence. Use this confidence score as a bonus for the self-supervised contrastive loss, forcing the model to preserve temporal coherence in the videos.
controls: baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations)
cost: estimated 3000 gpu-hours
prediction: The video discriminator helps improve the model's ability to capture sequential patterns in the videos, but may increase computational requirements and potentially degrade performance on non-sequential tasks.

action: revise 2
title: evaluating video discriminator for self-supervised pretraining
proposal: Dive deeper into understanding the effects of training with a video discriminator on visual foundation models, including an exploration of different discriminator architectures, such as convolutional, recurrent or transformer-based discriminators. Examine the performance of the models both on task-specific objectives (e.g., object recognition from videos) and on general visual quality metrics (e.g., SSIM, SROCC).
controls: baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations), video discriminator with no demographic influences
cost: estimated 2000 gpu-hours
prediction: One discriminator architecture performs better for sequence based video tasks, and another discriminative model structure is better fitting with overall enhanced image quality.

action: add
title: model-to-model distillation for unsupervised fine-tuning
proposal: Implement a model-to-model distillation framework that leverages the knowledge from pre-trained visual foundation models, similar to distillation in supervised learning but adapted for unsupervised fine-tuning. Introduce an additional teacher-student distillation loss, where the student model is the fine-tuning model and the teacher model is the pre-trained VFM. Use temperature schedules and loss balancing to adapt the distillation loss to the unsupervised setting.
controls: baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations), and study various temperature schedules and teacher-student weight balancing factor.
cost: estimated 2500 gpu-hours
prediction: The model-to-model distillation can be effective in transferring knowledge from the pre-trained VFM to the fine-tuning model, especially when the pre-trained model has a significantly larger capacity than the fine-tuning model. However, may have difficulty adapting to task-specific features.

action: revise 3
title: model-to-model distillation for unsupervised fine-tuning
proposal: Investigate the effect of tuning the teacher-student hyperparameters in the model-to-model distillation framework, including the temperature, balancing factor, and the choice of optimization algorithm for the student model. Analyze how different combinations of these hyperparameters influence the student model's performance on object recognition tasks from videos, and evaluate the sensitivity of the distillation process to these parameters.
controls: best-performing baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations)
cost: estimated 1500 gpu-hours
prediction: Optimal hyperparameters are discovered for model-to-model distillation based on large-scale hyperparameter search using Bayesian optimization. Balance is struck where both knowledge transfer from teacher increases downstream accuracy; and unstable optimization methods are avoided, and reliable student learning paradigm is found.

action: add
title: understanding the role of data mixing for unsupervised fine-tuning
proposal: Introduce a data mixing strategy, where the input videos are mixed with previously seen videos or generated videos with similar content, aiming to encourage the model to learn robust and generalizable features. Evaluate how different mixing strategies, such as introducing uniform noise or using reinforcement learning to adapt the mixing strategy, influence the performance of the fine-tuning model on object recognition tasks.
controls: best-performing baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations), model-to-model distillation with tuned hyperparameters
cost: estimated 3000 gpu-hours
prediction: mixing with real data improves recognition accuracy more than with artificially generated content mixed with the original video frames present within the domain at hand.

action: revise 4
title: understanding the role of data mixing for unsupervised fine-tuning
proposal: Investigate the effect of different mixing ratios and mixing strategies on the performance of the fine-tuning model, including the introduction of synthetic videos with Cartesian noise, small translations, or color jitter. Additionally, analyze the influence of different mixing strategies on the model's ability to generalize to unseen videos and its ability to capture task-specific features.
controls: best-performing baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations), model-to-model distillation with tuned hyperparameters, no data mixing
cost: estimated 2500 gpu-hours
prediction: Using the results from an optimization search for mixing strategies and optimal mixing ratios, that mixing technique offers robust learning even under the presence of noise, as demonstrated by extrapolated results.

action: add
title: urban driving scenario subset for evaluating model performance
proposal: Investigate the performance of the fine-tuned models on a specific subset of videos from the Urban Driving Scenario dataset, which includes videos with varying lighting conditions, weather, and driving directions. Evaluate how the different approaches (image-wise contrastive learning, self-supervised pretraining with video discriminator, and model-to-model distillation) generalize to this specific scenario and analyze their strengths and weaknesses in capturing task-specific features.
controls: best-performing baseline from proposal 1 (image-wise contrastive learning with augmentations), model-to-model distillation with tuned hyperparameters, and data mixing with optimal mixing ratios
cost: estimated 4000 gpu-hours
prediction: Model trained on diverse scenarios is able to generalise to urban driving setting with more nuanced change in scene recognition compared to models adapted through the opposite method.

action: add
title: implications and future work for visualization-based unsupervised fine-tuning
proposal: Discuss the theoretical implications of the experimental results and provide insights into the properties of visual foundation models under different unsupervised fine-tuning scenarios. Outline potential future research directions, focusing on geometric and data-efficient augmentations, hierarchical information representation, and hybrid methods combining multiple pre-training techniques.
controls: all experiments in current set, theoretical analysis
cost: negligible (literature review and analysis)
prediction: The results provide a comprehensive understanding of the strengths and limitations of each pre-training method and suggest promising future research directions for improving the efficiency and effectiveness of unsupervised fine-tuning approaches.

ACTION: ADD
title: evaluating contrastive learning on unlabeled videos for vfm adaptation
PROPOSAL: We will fine-tune a pre-trained VFM on unlabeled videos of objects, specifically using a variant of the SimCLR contrastive learning framework that optimizes an InfoNCE loss. The video frames will be taken from multiple views (e.g., top, side, back, etc.), allowing the VFM to learn about spatial invariances. We will evaluate this fine-tuned model's performance on object recognition from multi-view object-centric videos.
CONTROLS: We will compare to the standard supervised fine-tuning setup, as well as ablate the InfoNCE loss to see if a more basic form of contrastive loss (e.g., tripble loss) helps or hinders adaptation. We will also compare against a VFM that has continued self-supervised pretraining on the target dataset, but not supervised fine-tuning.
COST: 1000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect contrastive learning to adapt the VFM's representations to some extent, but the gain will be modest due to the lack of labeled data. The VFM may learn some basic visual features, such as object sizes or color criteria, but it will struggle to learn complex object relationships.

ACTION: ADD
title: using multi-object videos for negative sampling in vfm adaptation
PROPOSAL: We will extend the previous proposal by using multi-object videos as a source of negative samples in the contrastive learning process. Specifically, we'll take frames from different objects in the video and treat them as negatives, encouraging the VFM to distinguish between objects in the same scene. This will help the model learn a more nuanced understanding of object relationships.
CONTROLS: We will ablate the use of multi-object videos as negatives, and compare to a setup where all frames are treated as positives. We will also compare to a setup where we use a separate dataset of object images as negatives.
COST: 500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect multi-object videos to be an effective source of negatives, leading to improved adaptation performance on object recognition tasks. However, it may be challenging to balance the quality of negatives with the potential risk of overfitting if the negatives are too strong.

ACTION: ADD
title: incorporating temporal consistency for vfm adaptation on videos
PROPOSAL: We will modify the contrastive learning objective to incorporate temporal consistency, by encouraging the VFM to predict the same object representation from adjacent frames in a video. This will allow the model to learn about temporal invariances and capture the dynamic properties of objects.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline where the VFM is only fine-tuned on singleton frames, and against a variant where we use a recurrent neural network (RNN) to temporally process the frames before feeding them to the VFM.
COST: 1500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect incorporating temporal consistency to significantly improve the VFM's adaptation performance on videos, particularly for tasks that require motion understanding. However, the added temporal processing may come at the cost of increased computational complexity.

ACTION: REVISE
title: pushing the limits of self-supervised learning for vfm adaptation on videos with multi-object scenarios and temporal consistency
PROPOSAL: We will combine the ideas from the previous proposals, and fine-tune a pre-trained VFM on a dataset of videos with multi-object scenarios, incorporating temporal consistency to encourage the model to learn about both spatial and temporal invariances. We will use a variant of the InfoNCE loss as the objective function, and compare our results against state-of-the-art supervised fine-tuning methods.
CONTROLS: We will compare against ablations where we remove either the multi-object scenarios or the temporal consistency, and against a no-temporal-constraint baseline. We will also compare against a variant where we use online contrastive learning with a moving average of the encoder for incorporating temporal consistency.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect our approach to set a new state of the art for self-supervised learning on this problem, and demonstrate the potential of combining contrastive learning with spatial and temporal invariances for VFM adaptation on videos. However, the computational requirements may be challenging to meet for large-scale experiments, and the presence of multiple objects may lead to increased background noise.

ACTION: ADD
title: pruning the vfm for adaptation with mask r-cnn
PROPOSAL: We will fine-tune a pruned version of the VFM, obtained using mask R-CNN as a pruning agent. This will allow the model to selectively prune features that are not relevant for object recognition, and retain only those that are most informative. We will compare our results against a baseline where the VFM is pruned with a random mask.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline where the VFM is not pruned, and against a variant where we use a random mask to prune the model. We will also compare against a variant where we use a different pruning algorithm.
COST: 2000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect pruning the VFM to improve its adaptation performance on object recognition tasks, particularly on videos with cluttered backgrounds or complex scenes. However, the effectiveness of the pruning algorithm may depend on the specific task and dataset.

ACTION: ADD
title: leveraging video priors for vfm adaptation
PROPOSAL: We will incorporate video priors learned from a separate dataset of videos, to guide the adaptation process of the VFM. This will allow the model to leverage domain knowledge from a related but different domain, and make it more robust to distribution shifts in the adaptation task. We will use a variant of the ADMIT framework to learn these priors.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline where the VFM is adapted without any incorporation of video priors, and against a variant where we use a pre-trained VFM as the source of priors.
COST: 2500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect leveraging video priors to improve the VFM's adaptation performance on object recognition tasks, particularly on videos with complex scenes or objects. However, the effectiveness of the priors may depend on the quality of the source dataset for learning the priors.

action: add
title: continuation learning for preserving vfm's pre-trained knowledge during adaptation
PROPOSAL: We will modify the adaptation process to incorporate a continuation learning component, which will help preserve the VFM's pre-trained knowledge during adaptation. This will be achieved by adding a continuation task to the original adaptation task, and learning a separate set of parameters to optimize both tasks simultaneously.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline where the VFM is adapted without continuation learning, and against a variant where we use a continuation learning component with a different adaptation objective.
COST: 3000 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect continuation learning to improve the VFM's adaptation performance on object recognition tasks, particularly in scenarios where the pre-trained knowledge is critical for performance. However, the effectiveness of continuation learning may depend on the specific adaptation task and dataset.

action: add
title: investigating spatio-temporal attention for vfm adaptation on object-centric videos
PROPOSAL: We will modify the VFM's architecture to incorporate spatio-temporal attention mechanisms, which will allow the model to selectively attend to relevant regions and frames in the input video. This will be achieved by adding a spatio-temporal attention module to the VFM's architecture.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline where the VFM is adapted without spatio-temporal attention mechanisms, and against a variant where we use a different attention mechanism.
COST: 2800 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect spatio-temporal attention to improve the VFM's adaptation performance on object recognition tasks, particularly on videos with complex scenes or objects. However, the effectiveness of the attention mechanism may depend on the specific adaptation task and dataset.

action: add
title: evaluating the robustness of vfm adaptation under distribution shift
PROPOSAL: We will evaluate the robustness of the VFM adaptation process under distribution shift, by fine-tuning the VFM on a dataset with a different distribution from the original adaptation dataset. We will compare the performance of the adapted VFM on the shifted dataset against the original adaptation dataset.
CONTROLS: We will compare against a baseline where the VFM is not adapted on the shifted dataset, and against a variant where we use a different adaptation method that is more robust to distribution shift.
COST: 3500 GPU-hours
PREDICTION: We expect the VFM adaptation process to be less robust under distribution shift, and the adapted VFM to perform worse on the shifted dataset. However, the extent of the performance drop may depend on the specific adaptation method and the complexity of the distribution shift.

action: add
title: mitigating catastrophic forgetting in vfm adaptation through episodic training
PROPOSAL: We will modify the adaptation process to mitigate catastrophic forgetting, by incorporating episodic training methodology that maintains a memory of previous tasks and episodes, and gradually updates the VFM's parameters to avoid forgetting previously learned knowledge.
